cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing to the church in Corinth, and he's just said he disciplines himself so he won't be disqualified (1 Corinthians 9:27). Now he opens up the old family photo album: he doesn't want them unaware about “our forefathers.” Every last one of them was under the cloud.

cards.question: Paul says all their forefathers were under the cloud, and that they all passed through the ___.

cards.text: Paul says they were all baptized into Moses, Israel's leader, in the cloud and in the sea. Same cloud. Same sea. The WHOLE crowd.
And Paul's not done listing what they ALL got. They all ate the same spiritual food and drank the same spiritual drink, from a spiritual rock that went right along with them.

cards.question: Paul says the spiritual rock that went along with those forefathers was ___.
The cloud, the sea, the food and the drink went to ALL of those forefathers. True or false: Paul says God was pleased with most of them.

cards.text: Paul says most of them were struck down in the wilderness. Every one of them got the cloud, the sea, the food and the drink, and still most of them fell right there in the wilderness.

cards.question: Why does Paul say all of this happened to those forefathers?

answers.text: As examples to keep us from craving evil
To show how hard the wilderness could be
To explain why the cloud led them there

cards.text: Then Paul gets specific and quotes Exodus 32:6, from the time Israel made a golden calf (Exodus 32:4): “The people sat down to eat and drink and got up to indulge in revelry.”

cards.question: Paul uses that golden calf line to back up his first warning to the Corinthians. What is the warning?

cards.text: Next, Paul says we should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died. And we should not test Christ, as some of them did, and they were killed by snakes.
Paul's got one more warning from that same wilderness. Four warnings out of one camp. That's a LOT of lessons from one trip.

cards.question: What is Paul's fourth warning from the wilderness?

cards.text: Some of them complained and were killed by the destroying angel. Paul says all of this was written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.

cards.question: After all those warnings, Paul says the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to ___.

cards.text: Then Paul turns encouraging: no temptation has seized you except what is common to man. Whatever you're up against, friend, you are NOT the first, not the hundredth, not even CLOSE.

cards.question: Paul says God is faithful. True or false: Paul says God will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear.
When you are tempted, what does Paul say God will also provide so you can stand up under it?

cards.text: The history lesson's over, and Paul brings it home with one big word: therefore. He calls the Corinthians his beloved, and he tells them what to do about idolatry.

cards.question: After all those warnings from Israel's history, what does Paul tell his beloved to do about idolatry?

cards.text: Paul says he's speaking to reasonable people, so judge for yourselves. Friend, that's like setting the cookies on the counter and letting you taste for yourself.
Then he asks about the cup of blessing that they bless. Isn't it a participation in the blood of Christ?

cards.question: Paul asks the same kind of question about the bread they break. He asks if it's a participation in the ___ of Christ.
Paul says we who are many are one body. Why does he say that is?

answers.text: Because we all partake of the one loaf
Because we all follow the same apostle
Because we all live in the same city

cards.text: Then Paul brings the people of Israel back into it, this time eating the sacrifices from the altar.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the people of Israel who eat the sacrifices are fellow partakers in the altar.

cards.text: Then Paul asks a question of his own. Is he suggesting that food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?

cards.question: True or false: Paul answers his own question about idols with a yes.
Paul says the sacrifices of pagans are offered to ___, not to God.

cards.text: And Paul does not want them to be participants with demons. That is one guest list you do NOT want your name on.

cards.question: Paul says you cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too. What else does he say you cannot partake in from both the Lord and demons?
Paul ends with two questions. The first asks if they're trying to provoke the Lord to what?

cards.text: Then the second question: “Are we stronger than He?” Paul leaves that one sitting right there on the counter, and trust me, friend, this teaching isn't done yet.
